bibliographic.title: Operationalising ethics in artificial intelligence for healthcare: a framework for AI developers
bibliographic.authors: Pravik Solanki; John Grundy; Waqar Hussain
bibliographic.citation_apa: Solanki, P., Grundy, J., & Hussain, W. (2022). Operationalising ethics in artificial intelligence for healthcare: a framework for AI developers. AI and Ethics, 3(2), 223–240. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-022-00195-z

methodology.study_design: scoping review of ethical AI guidelines, frameworks and technical solutions used to construct a solution-based operational framework
methodology.sample_description: existing solutions of ethical AI guidelines, frameworks and technical solutions addressing human values in healthcare AI
methodology.technology_context: machine learning, natural language processing, NLP-driven chatbots, deep learning algorithms applied to clinical text, images and unstructured healthcare data

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article provides a healthcare-focused, developer-oriented ethics governance framework spanning data management, model development, deployment and monitoring, with brief references to NLP-driven chatbots and human-AI interaction. Provided text does not address large language models or dedicated conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, tracing, contestation or post-deployment operational learning, so it supports regulated AI governance themes but is not central evidence for LLM-based conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was supplied; confirm full-text coverage of conversational systems, monitoring practices, accountability mechanisms and absence of LLM-specific discussion before final inclusion coding.

appraisal.notes: Clear objective and appropriate scoping-review-plus-framework approach for operationalising ethics for healthcare AI developers. Adequacy of literature sampling and detailed review protocol are not fully evidenced in the supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is coherently presented and grounded in a stated scoping review, but the supplied text gives limited detail on review sampling and selection. Relevance to the review focus is moderate because governance and healthcare regulation are strong, while LLM-specific and conversational-governance content is peripheral in the provided evidence.

axial_codes: conversational AI as secondary use case
coding.theme: Operational ethics governance for healthcare AI developers
coding.subtheme: Lifecycle framework translating ethical principles into actionable technical and non-technical practices
rq_alignment: partial alignment to conversational systems via chatbot and human-AI interaction references
weak alignment to LLM-specific conversational governance

synthesis.main_claim: The authors propose a solution-based framework to operationalise ethics in healthcare AI for developers by collating actionable technical and non-technical practices across the full AI lifecycle.
synthesis.contribution: Moves beyond principle-based guidance by synthesising existing ethical AI guidelines, frameworks and technical solutions into developer-accessible recommendations covering data management, model development, deployment and monitoring.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for regulated healthcare AI governance, lifecycle controls, monitoring, transparency and human-AI interaction; not as central evidence for LLM-based conversational governance because LLMs and conversational-specific controls are not substantively addressed in the supplied text.
